title: Heterogeneous-arch probe + lightweight runtime kernel orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, low-overhead orchestrator that probes heterogeneous GPU/CPU kernels at request time to recommend per-request kernel choices. The feature must be sequence-length and architecture aware, minimize added latency during cold starts/prefill, and gracefully fall back to stable kernels. Deliverables: probe agent, cost model adapter, rollout plan, dashboards and safety gates.
comments: 2026-02-25 Maya Chen: Initial groom. Problem statement: We see 8-15% median token cost variance and 10-30% p99 latency differences across kernel implementations depending on model sequence-length and hardware generation (A100 v3 vs H100 vs consumer Ampere). Current static selection doesn't account for bursty seqlen distributions. Proposal: experiment with a lightweight probe that runs microbenchmarks (tiny prefill kernels) to warm a per-worker fingerprint and select kernel variant for subsequent prefill/decode requests.

2026-02-26 Ethan Rivera: Spike approved. Plan: (1) define probe microbench suite (prefill 64/256 tokens; decode 1/64); (2) build in-memory fingerprint store keyed by (model, device_fingerprint, seqlen_bucket); (3) cost model adapter retrieves historical metrics + microprobe results to rank candidate kernels; (4) decision policy: optimistic-exploit bandit with safety floor to avoid regressions.

2026-03-03 Internals: Microprobe design choices. We rejected full Bayes bandit per request due to CPU overhead. Chosen approach: episodic epsilon-greedy with decay and half-life, plus a deterministic safety policy that pins heavy-traffic routes to ensemble winners. Microprobe runs at worker start and periodically (every 15 minutes) when load allows. Avoid probing on tail latency-sensitive requests by sampling low-priority background traffic.

2026-03-05 Benchmarks: Local perf-run results for 'gpt-redwood-3b' on H100: flash-attn-fused shows 18% median decoding speedup for seqlen=1-32, but tiled-matmul has 9% advantage at seqlen>=256. Prefill microprobe (128 token prefill) correlates with decode kernels in 87% of cases; so using prefill-derived fingerprint is viable for decoding decisions. p99 regressions observed when switching mid-request — added constraint: kernel changes allowed only between prefill and decode, not mid-decode streams.

2026-03-07 Design note: Attention variant features to capture in cost model: memory-bandwidth pressure, shared-L2 occupancy, kv-cache size, tok-percentage-prefill, and architecture hints (sm_version, sm_count). We will record approximate device memory temp and GPU compute utilization from our telemetry to avoid choosing memory-intensive kernels on near-full devices.

2026-03-09 PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1429 implements microprobe harness and fingerprint store. Early review requests: @nora and @liam. CI notes: added microprobe unit tests and a simulation harness replicating mixed seqlen traces.

2026-03-10 QA notes: Synthetic trace runner with mixed workload (60% short decode, 30% short prefill, 10% long prefill) showed 7% average token-cost reduction and 6ms median latency improvement on H100 clusters; however cost savings reduced to 2% on older Ampere workers due to lack of flash-attn speedups. Action: add fallback policy that prefers stability over minor cost when p99 latency delta > 5%.

2026-03-11 Security & privacy review: Telemetry collected for decisioning contains model name, device fingerprint (SM/PCI IDs), and aggregated timing. Confirmed no customer input text is sent to probe; telemetry sampling at 0.1% for synthetic user traces and 100% for internal synthetic microbenchmarks. SRE requested an opt-out flag for customers running in Dedicated/Private.

2026-03-12 Next steps: rollout plan drafted. Phase 1: internal-only rollout on canary pool with 'probe=on' tag; monitor token-cost, median latency, and p99; abort threshold: any >10% p99 regression or >15% error spike. Phase 2: opt-in beta for 5 customers on Dedicated; Phase 3: automated rollouts with gradual traffic ramp (10->50->100%) and automatic rollback on safety gates. Add dashboards: kernel-choice distribution, probe success rate, delta-cpu/gpu-util, and per-route cost delta.

Follow-ups: consolidate cost model into runtime-telemetry adapter (ENG-24101), add user-configurable probe cadence in dedicated/private, and document known incompatibilities with quantized kernels (some kernels unsupported for int8 dims).
